newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Re-election tops agenda as Brazil Congress resumes.
newsitem.headline: Re-election tops agenda as Brazil Congress resumes.

text.p: Brazil's Congress is expected to begin returning to normal this week as deputies and senators return from campaigning in last week's municipal elections, with re-election the hottest issue.

A lower house committee to debate a proposed constitutional amendment allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, plus sitting state governors and mayors, the chance of a second term should be set up next week, a congressional official said.
Lower House President Luiz Eduardo Magalhaes would ask this week leaders of political parties to nominate their members of the committee, the official said.

Leaders of political parties allied to the government were quoted as saying they believed the committee would not vote on the proposal until after the second round of voting in the municipal elections on November 15.

Newspapers said Cardoso would meet with Magalhaes on Monday, the party leaders on Tuesday, and Miguel Arraes, the influential governor of Pernambuco state on Wednesday, to hammer out a stategy for getting the re-election amendment through Congress.
"This week will be one of low productivity and intense discussions," Michel Temer, lower house leader of the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) told O Estado de Sao Paulo.
With re-election taking up most of the government's attention, there is little chance of much progress this week with other reforms.
The administratitve reform may be put to a vote in its lower house committee next week, said the congressional official.
The reform would allow for the dismissal of currently unsackable civil servants in states and municipalities where payrolls accounts for more than 60 percent of receipts

A proposed reform of the tax system is scheduled to begin committee-level discussions October 16, while a watered-down version of the government's pension reform proposals is awaiting a rewrite in the Senate.
